concepts.def: A system in which no mass enters or leaves and no external resultant force acts. Conservation of momentum is stated by the specification for a closed system, and it is that condition which makes the total momentum before and after an event equal.

The name given to the statement that, in a closed system, the total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after the event. It applies to the total for the whole system, not to each object separately.

Anything that changes how the objects in a system are moving: a collision, objects sticking together, or an explosion pushing objects apart. Momentum is used as a model to describe and explain what happens in such an event.

An event in which objects initially at rest push each other apart. The total momentum before is zero, so the total momentum after must also be zero: the two objects move in opposite directions with momenta of equal size.

mcqs.q: The specification states conservation of momentum for a closed system. What is a closed system?
options: One in which the objects are all sealed inside a container, so that nothing can escape from it
One in which no mass enters or leaves and no resultant force acts on it from outside the system
One in which nothing is moving, so that the total momentum of the system stays equal to zero
One in which the objects touch each other, so that momentum can be passed from one to another
mcqs.explain: This is the condition under which the total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after it.

mcqs.q: In a closed system the total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after it. What is this called?
mcqs.explain: This is the name the specification gives to the statement in 4.5.7.2.

mcqs.q: Two skaters stand at rest on ice and push each other apart. Which statement about their momentum is correct?
options: They have equal and opposite momenta, so the total is still zero, as it was before the push
Both of the skaters are now moving, so the system has gained momentum from the push they gave
Each skater simply keeps the momentum it began with, which was zero for both
Their momenta add together, giving twice the momentum that one skater has on its own
mcqs.explain: The total momentum before the push is zero, and in a closed system the total after must also be zero.

mcqs.q: A moving trolley collides with a stationary trolley and slows down, while the second trolley moves off. Which description is correct?
options: Some momentum was destroyed in the collision, which is why the first trolley slowed down
Each trolley keeps the momentum it began with, since momentum is a conserved quantity
The momentum lost by the first trolley equals the momentum gained by the second, so the total is unchanged
The second trolley gains momentum but the first loses more, so the total falls in the collision
mcqs.explain: In a closed system the total momentum before the event equals the total momentum after it.
